title: GMAT Focus Edition: The One-Glance Format
summary: Three 45-minute sections, a 205–805 score, and two powers the old GMAT never gave you: choose your order and edit answers.

nodes.label: Data Insights

chunks.heading: Three equal sections, 45 minutes each
chunks.body: The GMAT Focus Edition has **three 45-minute sections — Quantitative Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Data Insights — for a total of 2 hours 15 minutes** (about an hour shorter than the old GMAT). Each section is **equally weighted** in your total score.
chunks.realExample: Unlike the old GMAT, there's no essay (AWA) and no separate Integrated Reasoning tacked on — Data Insights absorbed that role and now counts fully toward your score.
chunks.memoryHook: 3 sections × 45 min, all equal. No essay. Data Insights counts now.

chunks.heading: You choose the section order
chunks.body: You pick **which of the three sections to take first, second and third**. Play to your energy: **lead with your strongest section** to bank confidence, or your weakest while fresh — but decide your order in advance so you're not choosing under pressure.
chunks.realExample: A candidate who tightens up on Quant might do Verbal first to settle in; another might attack Quant first while sharpest. Rehearse your chosen order in every practice test.
chunks.memoryHook: Your order, your call. Pick a strategy and rehearse it — don't improvise on test day.

chunks.heading: You can bookmark and edit answers
chunks.body: Within each section you can **bookmark questions and change up to three answers** before time runs out (using the question review & edit screen). This rewards a **two-pass approach**: answer everything, flag the shaky ones, then revisit.
chunks.realExample: Unsure between two answers? Lock one in, bookmark it, and if you have time at the end, the review screen lets you reconsider up to three — a safety net the old GMAT never offered.
chunks.memoryHook: Bookmark + edit up to 3 per section. Answer all, flag doubts, revisit.

chunks.heading: It's adaptive and scored 205–805
chunks.body: The GMAT is **computer-adaptive** — each section adjusts difficulty to your performance — and your **total score runs 205–805** in 10-point steps, built from all three equally-weighted sections. Business schools compare **percentiles**, so check your target programme's typical range.
chunks.realExample: Because sections are equal, a lopsided profile (great Quant, weak Verbal) drags your total more than on the old GMAT — balance across all three now matters.
chunks.memoryHook: 205–805, adaptive, 3 equal sections. Balance beats one heroic section.

recall.q: What are the three GMAT Focus sections and how long is each?
recall.a: Quantitative Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Data Insights — each 45 minutes, 2 hours 15 minutes total.

recall.q: What two flexibilities does GMAT Focus give test takers?
recall.a: You can choose the order of the three sections and bookmark and edit up to three answers per section.

recall.q: What is the GMAT Focus total score range?
recall.a: 205 to 805, in 10-point increments, from three equally-weighted sections.

recall.q: What happened to the essay (AWA) and Integrated Reasoning?
recall.a: The essay was removed and Integrated Reasoning evolved into the Data Insights section, which now counts fully toward the score.

recall.q: Why does a balanced profile matter more on GMAT Focus?
recall.a: All three sections are equally weighted, so a weak section drags the total more than on the old GMAT.
